# witgen

WIT JSON → Soil bindings.

`wasm-tools` is the parser. It happens in the build/tool layer, not at runtime
and not in Loam:

```sh
wasm-tools component wit tests/wit/wasi-stdio -j > /tmp/wit.json
```

The generator is Soil:

```sh
soil-run --prelude core/prelude.soil --call main tools/witgen/main.soil \
  --arg "$(cat /tmp/wit.json)" \
  --arg "wasi:cli@0.2.4" \
  > std/bindings/wasi-cli.generated.soil
```

The second argument selects a package from a multi-package WIT resolution.

Generated files start with:

```text
; @generated by tools/witgen/main.soil from wasm-tools component wit -j.
; DO NOT EDIT. Regenerate with `tend witgen`.
```

The output uses canonical interface keys:

```lisp
(host-call "wasi:io/streams" "input-stream.blocking-read" (list self len))
```

That keeps `input-stream` and `output-stream` methods from colliding.

## tend

`tend.soil` declares `witgen` as a project command. `tend` decides what to run;
the host runs `wasm-tools` and the Soil generator. That keeps WIT parsing out of
Loam and out of the Soil runtime.
